briefing.headline: US-China AI compute sanctions tighten as o4-preview nears 85% on GPQA

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The frontier race accelerates with new model releases from OpenAI and DeepSeek while regulatory scrutiny mounts on export controls. Compute shortages are reshaping alliances as nations prioritize sovereign AI infrastructure. Prompt injection vulnerabilities continue to plague deployments across sectors.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released o4-preview achieving new highs on coding benchmarks while Anthropic's Claude 4.1 focuses on long-context reasoning. DeepSeek-V4 undercuts pricing at $0.08 per million tokens, forcing Meta to accelerate Llama 4 open weights. xAI's Grok-3 training run completes on Memphis supercluster.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New EU AI Act enforcement actions target autonomous agent deployments. Researchers disclose zero-day in multi-agent orchestration frameworks.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: TSMC begins 2nm volume production for AI accelerators with NVIDIA securing 60% allocation. Microsoft announces $15B data center expansion in Texas tied to OpenAI workloads. Google TPU v6 pods achieve 40% efficiency gains over prior generation.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will export controls on advanced chips slow China's frontier progress enough to create a durable US lead through 2028?
